method_notes: PRIMARY SOURCE: examside (questions.examside.com) chapter-wise PYQ lists. For every JEE Main chapter page I read its 'PYQ Statistics' table (total questions and average per paper per year) and, for 2019-2026, recounted questions from the per-question shift labels; the two agree. Summed over all examside chapters the yearly totals equal exactly papers x questions-per-paper (2019: 16 shifts x 30 = 480; 2020: 16 x 25 = 400; 2021: 26 x 30 = 780; 2022: 23 x 30 = 690; 2023: 24 x 30 = 720; 2024: 20 x 30 = 600; 2025: 19 x 25 = 475; 2026: 19 x 25 = 475), so every question is tagged to exactly one chapter. main.by_year = examside total for that chapter / number of shifts that year. For 2021-2024 the paper had 30 chemistry questions (10 numericals, of which only 5 had to be attempted), and examside counts all 30, so per-shift values for those years are on a 30-question base; 2020 and 2025-2026 are on a 25-question base. main.avg_questions_per_shift = 0.7 x mean(2024, 2025, 2026) + 0.3 x mean(2019-2023), to weight the post-2024-syllabus papers. For the nine chapters removed from the Main syllabus in 2024, avg = mean(2024-2026) only (about 0), because the old numbers no longer apply; their 2019-2023 values are still kept in by_year. advanced.by_year = examside count of questions tagged to the chapter across Paper 1 + Paper 2 (counted from per-question labels; totals check: 2019 36, 2020 36, 2021 38, 2022 36, 2023 34, 2024 34, 2025 32, 2026 34). advanced.avg_questions = mean of non-null years. Chapter mapping from examside: Gaseous State -> chem-states-of-matter; Chemical Kinetics and Nuclear Chemistry -> chem-chemical-kinetics; Periodic Table & Periodicity -> chem-periodic-table; Isolation of Elements -> chem-metallurgy; Salt Analysis -> chem-qualitative-analysis; Basics of Organic Chemistry -> chem-goc (it also contains isomerism and nomenclature questions); Compounds Containing Nitrogen -> chem-amines. examside has no Advanced 'Environmental Chemistry' chapter, and because its Advanced totals add up exactly, environmental chemistry is recorded as 0 there. CROSS-CHECKS: JEE Main 2025 Session 1 (10 shifts) per-chapter counts from CollegeDekho and from the PW/Vedantu table (Jan + Apr 2025) agree with examside within about 1-3 questions per session for coordination, thermodynamics, kinetics, electrochemistry, mole concept, atomic structure, biomolecules, hydrocarbons, haloalkanes, solutions and the equilibrium chapters (e.g. coordination Jan 2025: examside 20, CollegeDekho 19, PW 18; thermodynamics 17/17/15). Bigger disagreements, which come from where each source draws chapter lines: chemical bonding (examside 9 vs CollegeDekho 13 vs PW 8 in Jan 2025), periodic table (examside 28 vs PW 20 for all of 2025), alcohols (examside 7 vs PW 15 for 2025), p-block (examside 10 vs PW 19 for 2025), redox (examside 7 vs PW 3), amines (examside 22 vs PW 19). PW's 'Some Basic Principles and Techniques' (20 in Jan 2025) equals examside GOC (16) + practical organic (4). JEE Advanced: Allen's 2023 chapter table and Adarsh Barnwal's 2025 table agree with examside on most chapters (e.g. 2023 thermodynamics 4/4; 2025 p-block 3/3, coordination 2/2, electrochemistry 2/2, salt analysis 2/2). SPLITS: (1) p-Block. examside lumps groups 13-18. I sorted each Main 2021-2026 and Advanced 2019-2026 p-block question by the elements and compounds in its text (keyword/formula matching, plus reading every ambiguous 2021-2026 Main question and every Advanced question by hand). Questions that span both groups or are general p-block questions were left out of both chapters. Unassigned Main counts: 2021 7, 2022 4, 2023 4, 2024 9, 2025 1, 2026 2; Advanced: 2020 2 (so 2020 is null), 2022 2, 2026 1. Main 2019-2020 are null because too many questions had formulas only as images. These values are marked source_type 'estimate'. (2) Aldehydes/ketones vs carboxylic acids. examside, PW and Vedantu all merge these chapters, and most questions are reaction schemes drawn as images, so I could not split them. Merged examside Main per-shift values: 2019 1.81, 2020 1.44, 2021 1.65, 2022 1.30, 2023 1.25, 2024 1.55, 2025 1.37, 2026 1.84 (weighted avg 1.56). Merged Advanced totals: 2019 4, 2020 2, 2021 1, 2022 1, 2023 3, 2024 6, 2025 1, 2026 6. The only split counts found: CollegeDekho Main Jan 2025 (Aldehydes and Ketones 10, Carboxylic Acid Derivatives 3, over 10 shifts, giving 1.0 and 0.3 per shift; this is Session 1 only). For Advanced: Adarsh Barnwal 2025 (Carbonyl 1, Carboxylic acid & derivative 3) and Allen 2023 (Carbonyl 1; carboxylic acids folded into a 5-question 'mixed' group, so null). The per-chapter averages for these two chapters rest on these few data points only. (3) Isomerism. No source counts it separately for Main or Advanced; it sits inside GOC / 'Basics of Organic Chemistry', so it is null. A keyword scan of examside GOC finds roughly 5-16 identifiable isomerism/stereo questions a year in Main 2024-2026. That figure is indicative only and is not used. high_yield = in roughly the top 30% by main.avg_questions_per_shift or advanced.avg_questions (coordination, GOC, chemical bonding, amines, mole concept, d/f block, thermodynamics, kinetics, electrochemistry, hydrocarbons, carbonyl chapters, p-block 15-18). roi is a judgement based on the usual coaching view of chapter length and difficulty against these counts. confidence: high = examside plus at least one other source agree closely; medium = examside only, or sources disagree on chapter boundaries; low = derived split or very thin data.
uncertainties: Removed-from-Main chapters that still had questions tagged in Main 2024-2026 (examside): Surface Chemistry 2 in 2024 (Tyndall-effect assertion-reason, 31 Jan S1; 'adsorption principle used in which purification method', 4 Apr S2, which is really chromatography); Chemistry in Everyday Life 2 in 2024 (saponification/soap, 1 Feb S2; uses of CCl4/freons/DDT, 6 Apr S1, which is really NCERT haloalkanes); s-Block 1 in 2024 (flame colour assertion-reason, 6 Apr S2); States of Matter 1 in 2025 (van der Waals constant 'a' order, 7 Apr S1); Metallurgy 1 in 2025 (example of calcination, 28 Jan S2). CollegeDekho's Jan 2025 table also lists 1 'States of Matter' question. Most are borderline topics that the current syllabus keeps under other chapters, but they are real questions.
chem-isomerism: no per-chapter counts in any source for Main or Advanced (always merged into GOC); all values null.

chem-aldehydes-ketones and chem-carboxylic-acids: Main values come from CollegeDekho Jan 2025 Session 1 only; Advanced values only from Allen 2023 and Adarsh Barnwal 2025. All other years null. The Advanced average for carboxylic acids (3.0) is a single year and should not be read as a stable figure; the merged examside average for both chapters together is about 3.0 per year.

chem-p-block-13-14 / chem-p-block-15-18: split by my own classification of examside question text (estimate). Main 2019-2020 and Advanced 2020 are null; some general p-block questions are assigned to neither chapter.

Main 2021-2024 per-shift values are on a 30-question paper (including 5 optional numericals) and 2025-2026 on 25 questions, so before 2025 the numbers run a little high compared with what a candidate actually had to attempt.

Chapter boundaries differ between sources (bonding vs periodic table vs p-block, alcohols vs aromatic compounds, GOC vs practical organic vs salt analysis). Values follow examside's tagging, which is one site's editorial classification, not an official one.
No independent full-year chemistry chapter count was found for JEE Main 2026 or for JEE Main 2019-2024. Those years rest on examside alone, with partial agreement from PW's 5-year percentage table.
JEE Advanced chapter counts for 2019-2022, 2024 and 2026 come from examside only; Allen (2023) and Adarsh Barnwal (2025) were the only cross-checks found.
chem-environmental-chemistry Advanced = 0 because examside tags no Advanced chemistry question to it (its Advanced totals add up exactly), not because a source states 0.
